mainTopic: Two reasons for the same delay in eating תרומה, and a wife's earnings (מעשה ידיה) in exchange for her support (מזונות)
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion about when an engaged woman may eat תרומה. According to רב שמואל בר יהודה, both rulings worry about a hidden defect (סימפון). They differ only on whether a check done by the groom's female relatives (בדיקת חוץ) counts. A new משנה then teaches that a husband who consecrates his wife's earnings cannot stop her from working and supporting herself. רבי מאיר and רבי יוחנן הסנדלר disagree about the extra she earns. רב rules that a wife may refuse support and keep her earnings, because support is the main part of the arrangement. The גמרא defends this ruling against a ברייתא, and then shows that the משנה cannot prove it. ריש לקיש disagrees with רב: he explains רבי מאיר by saying the husband can force his wife to work, so it is as if he consecrated her hands. Finally, רב and שמואל argue with רב אדא בר אהבה about when the extra becomes holy. רב פפא narrows their dispute to a husband who gives food but no spending money, and the explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If both rulings share one reason, what is the difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: According to רב שמואל בר יהודה, the earlier and later rulings both come from worry about סימפון. So what do they disagree about?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רב שמואל בר יהודה, the first ruling is because of סימפון and the later ruling is also because of סימפון. So what is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב שמואל בר יהודה's explanation. It asks how two different rulings can rest on the very same reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, there was a first ruling and a later court's ruling about when an engaged woman may eat תרומה. If both are worried about the same thing, a hidden defect that could cancel the marriage, we need to find where they actually part ways. This question sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A hidden defect that could cancel the marriage after the fact
The first (earlier) ruling
The later ruling
What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: But according to Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda,
the first ruling is because of a hidden defect
phrases.notes: The first ruling is the earlier version of the משנה, about when an engaged woman may eat תרומה.

phrases.english: and the later ruling is also because of a hidden defect,
what is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of why engaged women do not eat תרומה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical point of disagreement between two rulings that share one reason

steps.title: They disagree about whether a check by his female relatives counts
steps.stepSummary: The difference is בדיקת חוץ. One side holds that it counts as a real check, and the other holds that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is a check done from the outside. One Sage holds that an outside check counts as a check. The other Sage holds that an outside check does not count as a check.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Both rulings worry about סימפון, but they disagree about whether a check done by his female relatives is good enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ruling holds that the outside check counts. So once the wedding date arrives, there is no longer a worry about a hidden defect. The later ruling holds that the outside check does not count, so the worry remains until the חופה.

keyTerms.meaning: An outside check, done by the groom's female relatives rather than by the groom himself
It counts as a real check

steps.whatToRemember: Two rulings can share the very same worry and still disagree about what is enough to remove it.

phrases.english: The difference between them is an outside check.
phrases.notes: A check done for him by his female relatives, which can only be a quick look from the outside.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: בְּדִיקַת חוּץ — שְׁמָהּ בְּדִיקָה.
phrases.english: One Sage holds: an outside check counts as a check.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: בְּדִיקַת חוּץ — לֹא שְׁמָהּ בְּדִיקָה.
phrases.english: And the other Sage holds: an outside check does not count as a check.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about whether בדיקת חוץ counts as a real check

steps.title: The new משנה: a husband who consecrates his wife's earnings
steps.stepSummary: A husband's attempt to make his wife's earnings הקדש does not stop her from working and supporting herself. רבי מאיר and רבי יוחנן הסנדלר disagree about the extra she earns.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man consecrates his wife's earnings, she may still work and support herself from them. As for the extra: רבי מאיר says it is הקדש, and רבי יוחנן הסנדלר says it is not holy.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with a husband who tries to give his wife's future work to the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, a wife's earnings belong to her husband. Even so, his act of consecrating them does not take away what she needs to support herself. The argument is only about the extra beyond what she owes him: רבי מאיר says the extra becomes holy, and רבי יוחנן הסנדלר says it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: His wife's earnings, meaning the work she produces
Property made holy and given to the בית המקדש
The extra she earns beyond what she must produce
Ordinary, non-holy property
She works and supports herself from it

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who consecrates his wife's earnings —
she may work and support herself.
As for the extra, Rabbi Meir says: it is consecrated,
Rabbi Yochanan the Cobbler says: it is non-sacred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband's consecration does not stop her from supporting herself. רבי מאיר says the extra is הקדש, and רבי יוחנן הסנדלר says it is חולין.

steps.title: A wife may give up support and keep her own earnings
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a wife may refuse her husband's support in order to keep her earnings. The reason is that support is the main part of the deal, and his right to her earnings exists only to prevent bad feelings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב: A woman may tell her husband, 'I will not be supported by you, and I will not work for you.' He holds that when the רבנן set this up, her support was the main part, and her earnings went to him only to prevent bad feelings. So if she says, 'I will not be supported and I will not work,' she has the right to do so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה with a rule from רב. A wife can cancel the whole support-for-earnings arrangement if she wants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן mainly made the arrangement for her benefit, by obligating the husband to support her. They gave him her earnings only so he would not resent supporting her while she kept her money. Since the arrangement exists for her benefit, she may choose to give it up.

keyTerms.meaning: I will not be supported, and I will not work for you
Support, meaning food and other living needs
The main part
Bad feelings or resentment
She has the right to choose this

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, the husband's support is the main part of the deal, and his right to her earnings comes second. So the wife can give up both.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sides: the husband cannot say 'I will not support you, so keep your earnings.' The choice belongs to the wife.
steps.whyThisMatters: This view of what is main and what is secondary in the arrangement shapes how the rest of the סוגיא will read the משנה.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Huna said that Rav said:
A woman may say to her husband:
"I will not be supported and I will not work."
phrases.notes: "I will not work" means "you won't get my earnings." She keeps whatever she makes.

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר: כִּי תַּקִּינוּ רַבָּנַן מְזוֹנֵי — עִיקָּר,
phrases.english: He holds: when the Sages instituted support, it was the main thing,
and her earnings were given to him because of animosity.
phrases.notes: He means: so the husband wouldn't resent supporting her while she kept her own money.

phrases.english: So when she says "I will not be supported and I will not work" —
she has the right to do so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wife may give up her support and keep her own earnings, because support is the main part of the arrangement and the husband's right to her earnings only prevents resentment.

steps.title: A teaching that seems to make earnings the main part of the deal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling with a ברייתא that says support was set up in exchange for earnings.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: The Sages set up her support in exchange for her earnings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's ruling from step 4 by quoting a teaching that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said support is the main part of the deal, so the wife may give it up. This ברייתא says 'support in exchange for earnings,' which sounds like earnings are the main part and support only comes because of them. If so, the wife should not be able to cancel the deal on her own.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages set up a rule (a rabbinic enactment)
In exchange for

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
They instituted sustenance
in exchange for her earnings!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning given in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that support is the main part of the deal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording 'support in exchange for earnings' makes earnings the main part, so the wife could not give up support to keep her earnings.

steps.title: Reverse the wording of the teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by reading the ברייתא the other way around: earnings in exchange for support.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: They set up her earnings in exchange for her support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the wording is reversed, support is the main part of the deal and the husband's right to earnings comes because of it. That matches רב's ruling exactly, so the challenge is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (the גמרא changes the wording)
Food and support the husband gives his wife

phrases.english: Say:
They instituted her earnings
in exchange for sustenance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא makes earnings the main part of the deal
steps.terutzMaskana: The correct reading makes support the main part, which fits רב

steps.title: A possible proof from the husband who makes her earnings הקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the case from step 3 supports רב, if that case is about a wife who is being supported.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this supports him: If a man makes his wife's earnings הקדש, she may still work and feed herself. Isn't this about a wife whom he supports?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to bring a proof for רב's ruling from the case quoted in step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the husband is supporting her. Then his הקדש should work, because her earnings belong to him. Yet she keeps working and eating from them. This would show that she can refuse his support and keep her earnings, just as רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say this supports him (introduces a possible proof)
Isn't it? (the גמרא suggests a way to read the source)
A wife who receives support from her husband

phrases.english: Let us say that this supports him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' means רב, whose ruling from step 4 is being tested.

phrases.english: One who consecrates his wife's earnings
she may work and eat from it.
Is it not about one who is sustained?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב, the גמרא looks for positive support
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that a wife may refuse support and keep her earnings
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case from step 3: the husband who makes his wife's earnings הקדש

steps.title: The case may be a wife who gets no support
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the case may be about a wife whom the husband does not support.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is about a wife who is not being supported.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof by reading the case another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband is not supporting her, then of course her earnings are not his to make הקדש. On that reading, the case says nothing about whether a wife can refuse support. So it is no proof for רב.

keyTerms.meaning: About a wife who is not receiving support

phrases.english: No, it is about one who is not sustained.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof; רב's ruling itself still stands
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the wife was being supported, but the case may be about a wife who is not

steps.title: Why teach something so obvious?
steps.stepSummary: If she gets no support, it is obvious she keeps her earnings; even a Hebrew slave must be fed, all the more so a wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is about a wife who is not supported, why does it need to be said? Even the view that a master may tell his slave 'Work for me, but I will not feed you' applies only to a Canaanite slave, about whom the Torah does not write 'with you.' But a Hebrew slave, about whom it is written 'with you,' must be fed. All the more so a man's wife!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading from step 8: if the wife gets no support, the teaching would be telling us something obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says a Hebrew slave is 'with you,' so his master must feed him. A wife is owed support even more surely. So a husband who does not feed her obviously has no claim to her earnings, and a teaching would not need to say so.

keyTerms.meaning: Why say it? (it seems obvious)
A non-Jewish slave
A Jewish slave who works for a set time
All the more so

steps.confusionAlert: The slave cases are not the topic here. They are only a comparison to show that a wife who gets no support obviously keeps her earnings.

phrases.english: If it is about one who is not sustained,
why does it need to be said?
Even according to the one who says
a master can say to the slave
"Work for me, and I will not feed you"
that applies only to a Canaanite slave,
about whom "with you" is not written,
but a Hebrew slave,
about whom "with you" is written
no; and all the more so his wife!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading given in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the case is about a wife who is not supported
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reasoning from the Hebrew slave shows that an unsupported wife obviously keeps her earnings, so there would be no need to teach it.

steps.title: The real new point is the argument about the extra earnings
steps.stepSummary: The first part was taught only to set up the next part: the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יוחנן הסנדלר about her extra earnings.
steps.simpleTranslation: The later part of the teaching was the reason it was needed: About the extra earnings, רבי מאיר says they are הקדש, and רבי יוחנן הסנדלר says they are not holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the first part of the teaching really is obvious, but it was needed to lead into the later part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea is in the argument about the extra she earns beyond what she needs to live on. So the reading from step 8, a wife who gets no support, can stand. This means the case gives no proof for רב.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part is why it was needed
The extra, what is left over
Not holy, ordinary property

steps.whatToRemember: רב's ruling survives the challenge from the ברייתא once its wording is reversed. But the case of the husband who makes her earnings הקדש cannot prove it, since that case may be about a wife who gets no support. The point of that case is really the argument over the extra earnings.

phrases.english: The latter clause was necessary for him:
the surplus: Rabbi Meir says it is consecrated,
phrases.notes: 'Surplus' means what she earns beyond what she needs to feed herself.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan the Cobbler says it is not sacred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: The first part is obvious, but it is needed to set up the later part
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A teaching about an unsupported wife would be pointless
steps.terutzMaskana: The teaching is needed for the argument about the extra earnings, so the reading from step 8 holds

steps.title: ריש לקיש's reason for רבי מאיר's ruling
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says רבי מאיר's ruling is not based on consecrating a דבר שלא בא לעולם. Instead, because the husband can force his wife to work, it is as if he consecrated her hands, which already exist. This disagrees with רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with ריש לקיש. ריש לקיש said: Don't say רבי מאיר's reason is that he holds a person can consecrate something not yet in the world. Rather, his reason is this: since the husband can force her to work, it is as if he told her, 'Your hands are consecrated to the One Who made them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings ריש לקיש's explanation of רבי מאיר's view from the משנה, and notes that it disagrees with רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש says the husband can force his wife to work. That means she cannot say 'I won't take support and I won't work,' which is exactly what רב allowed. He also moves רבי מאיר's reason away from consecrating future earnings. Instead, the consecration falls on her hands, which exist right now.

keyTerms.meaning: It disagrees with
Something that does not exist yet
To force her
Your hands are consecrated to the One Who made them

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the question of whether a wife may refuse support and refuse to work is a real disagreement. רב says she may; ריש לקיש says the husband can force her.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Reish Lakish.
phrases.notes: "This" is רב's ruling that a wife may say 'I won't take support and I won't work.'

phrases.english: For Reish Lakish said:
Do not say that the reason of Rabbi Meir
is because he holds

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם מַקְדִּישׁ דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: that a person can consecrate something that has not yet come into the world.
Rather, the reason of Rabbi Meir is:
since he can force her to produce her earnings,
he is considered as if he said to her:
"Let your hands be consecrated to the One Who made them."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 10 brought up the dispute about her extra earnings. Now the גמרא explains רבי מאיר's side through ריש לקיש, and shows this goes against רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, the husband can force his wife to work. So consecrating her earnings is treated as consecrating her hands, which already exist.

steps.title: But he never said those words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the husband only consecrated her earnings. He never said 'Let your hands be consecrated.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But he did not say that to her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש: how can we treat the husband as saying words he never said?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband said 'her earnings,' not 'her hands.' ריש לקיש's explanation seems to put words into his mouth.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely (opens a challenge)
Like this, this way

phrases.english: But he did not say this to her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording ריש לקיש gave in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that the husband is treated as saying 'Let your hands be consecrated'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: We should judge a person by what he actually said, and he only spoke about her earnings.

steps.title: A person does not speak for nothing
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that a person does not say words for no reason. So we read the husband's words in a way that works: as consecrating her hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since we have heard that רבי מאיר said 'A person does not say things for nothing,' the husband is treated as if he said to her, 'Let your hands be consecrated to the One Who made them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by using a known rule of רבי מאיר: we assume a person means his words to have some effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Consecrating earnings that don't exist yet might not work. So we read the husband's words in the way that does work: consecrating her hands. This rule comes from רבי מאיר himself, so it fits his view.

keyTerms.meaning: A person does not say things for nothing
We have heard (we know from elsewhere)

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּשָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּאָמַר:
phrases.english: Since we have heard that Rabbi Meir said:
A person does not say his words for nothing,
he is considered as if he said to her:
"Let your hands be consecrated to the One Who made them."

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּשָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings in a general rule of the same תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We go only by the husband's exact words, which were about her earnings.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר reads a person's words so that they take effect. So 'her earnings' is read as 'her hands.'

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי מאיר allows things not yet in the world
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does רבי מאיר really hold that one cannot act on a דבר שלא בא לעולם? A ברייתא says that in betrothals that can only take effect later, רבי מאיר rules she is betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי מאיר really hold that a person cannot consecrate something not yet in the world? But a ברייתא teaches: if a man says to a woman, 'You are betrothed to me after I convert,' or 'after you convert,' or 'after I am freed,' or 'after you are freed,' or 'after your husband dies,' or 'after your sister dies,' or 'after your יבם does חליצה for you,' רבי מאיר says: she is betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש. He suggested that רבי מאיר does not hold one can act on a דבר שלא בא לעולם, but a ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר does hold this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In every case in the ברייתא, the קידושין cannot work right now; they can only work in the future. Yet רבי מאיר says they work. So רבי מאיר does allow acting on something not yet in the world, and ריש לקיש's 'don't say that' seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothed
That I will convert
That I will be freed (from slavery)
Will perform חליצה

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Meir hold

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם מַקְדִּישׁ דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם?
phrases.english: that a person cannot consecrate something not yet in the world?
But it was taught: One who says to a woman:
"You are betrothed to me after I convert,"
or: "after you convert,"
"after I am freed," "after you are freed,"
"after your husband dies," or "after your sister dies,"
phrases.notes: Your sister: he is married to her sister, so he can't marry this woman until his wife dies.

phrases.english: or: "after your yavam performs chalitza for you,"
Rabbi Meir says: she is betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר אֵין אָדָם מַקְדִּישׁ דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to step 11 and challenges ריש לקיש's 'don't say' from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's suggestion that רבי מאיר's reason is not 'one can consecrate a דבר שלא בא לעולם'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא shows רבי מאיר lets קידושין take effect on a future situation, which means he does hold of acting on a דבר שלא בא לעולם.

steps.title: The ברייתא proves it, but our משנה does not
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא, yes, we learn that רבי מאיר allows a דבר שלא בא לעולם. But from our משנה alone we cannot prove it, because it can be explained another way.
steps.simpleTranslation: From that ברייתא, yes, we can learn it. From this משנה, we cannot learn it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what ריש לקיש really meant. He did not deny that רבי מאיר holds this; he only said our משנה is not the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש agrees that רבי מאיר holds one can act on a דבר שלא בא לעולם, as the ברייתא shows. His point is narrower: our משנה can be explained by the 'hands' reason. So the משנה alone does not prove רבי מאיר's view on this.

keyTerms.meaning: From that one (the ברייתא)
Yes
There is nothing to learn from it

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש agrees that רבי מאיר holds one can act on a דבר שלא בא לעולם. He only says our משנה can be explained another way: the husband can force her to work, so it is as if he consecrated her hands. That forcing is why ריש לקיש disagrees with רב.
steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not saying רבי מאיר disagrees with acting on a דבר שלא בא לעולם. He is only saying our משנה is not the place to prove it.

phrases.english: From that one (the ברייתא), yes, we can learn it;
from this one (our משנה), there is nothing to learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵהַהִיא אִין מֵהָא לֵיכָּא לְמִשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 by narrowing what ריש לקיש meant.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the claim: it is about what this source proves, not about רבי מאיר's actual view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש was denying that רבי מאיר allows acting on a דבר שלא בא לעולם.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר does allow it (as the ברייתא shows); ריש לקיש only said our משנה cannot prove it.

steps.title: When does the extra become holy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי מאיר's ruling from the משנה that the extra earnings are הקדש, then asks at what point they become holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'The extra earnings, רבי מאיר says they are הקדש.' The גמרא asks: When do they become holy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a new line of the משנה about the extra earnings (מותר) and asks a timing question. This step sets up the dispute that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we discussed why רבי מאיר says the husband's consecration works at all. Now the question is different: once we accept that the extra is holy, does it become holy right away or only later?

keyTerms.meaning: The extra, meaning the earnings left over beyond what is needed
Consecrated property that belongs to the בית המקדש
When?
Becomes holy (consecrated)

phrases.english: The extra: Rabbi Meir says it is consecrated.
When does it become holy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from why רבי מאיר's consecration works to when it takes effect.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The point in time at which the extra earnings become הקדש according to רבי מאיר.

steps.title: After her death or during her life
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל say the extra becomes holy only after the wife's death. רב אדא בר אהבה says it becomes holy while she is alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל both say: the extra becomes holy after her death. רב אדא בר אהבה says: the extra becomes holy during her life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the timing question with two opinions that disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that רבי מאיר makes the extra holy. They argue only about timing. רב and שמואל delay it until after the wife dies. רב אדא בר אהבה says it takes effect right away, while she is still living.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them
After death
During life, while alive

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel, who both say:
The extra becomes holy after death.
phrases.notes: He means after the wife's death.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
The extra becomes holy during life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 with two opposing opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב and שמואל: after the wife's death. רב אדא בר אהבה: while she is alive.

steps.title: If he gives her food and spending money, why wait?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks what case they argue about. If the husband gives her both food and a weekly מעה כסף, there is no reason to wait until her death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא thought about it: In what case are they arguing? If you say it is where he gives her food and also gives her a silver מעה for her needs, then what is the reason of the one who says it becomes holy only after death?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא tries to pin down the exact case of the dispute. He shows that the first possible case does not fit רב and שמואל's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband gives his wife everything he owes her, her earnings fully belong to him. So he should be able to consecrate the extra right away. That makes it hard to explain רב and שמואל, who wait until after her death.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought about it, he was puzzled by it
In what case?
Food, support
A small silver coin given to the wife for her other needs

phrases.english: Rav Pappa thought about it: In what case?
If you say it is where he gives her food
and gives her a silver ma'a for her needs —
what is the reason of the one who says
it becomes holy after death?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָוֵי בַּהּ רַב פָּפָּא: בְּמַאי? אִילֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what case the dispute in step 17 is about, and attacks the first option.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רב and שמואל, if the case is a husband who gives both food and a מעה כסף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When the husband meets all his duties, he fully owns her earnings, so the extra should be holy at once and not only after her death.

steps.title: If he gives her nothing, why holy during her life?
steps.stepSummary: The second possible case is that the husband gives neither food nor a מעה כסף. Then it is hard to explain רב אדא בר אהבה, who says the extra is holy during her life.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if it is where he does not give her food and does not give her a silver מעה for her needs, then what is the reason of the one who says it becomes holy during her life?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא tries the opposite case. That case does not fit the other opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband gives her nothing, she has to support herself from her own work. Her earnings are needed for her own living, so it is unclear there will be any extra at all. That makes it hard to say the extra becomes holy while she is alive.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather (introduces the other option)
When he does not provide

phrases.english: But rather, where he does not give her food

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מַעֲלֶה לָהּ מָעָה כֶּסֶף לִצְרָכֶיהָ —
phrases.english: and does not give her a silver ma'a for her needs —
what is the reason of the one who says
it becomes holy during life?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries the opposite case and shows it does not fit the other opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רב אדא בר אהבה, if the case is a husband who gives her nothing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When she must support herself, she may need all her earnings, so there is no clear extra that could be holy during her lifetime.

steps.title: The middle case: food but no spending money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the dispute is about a husband who gives her food but no מעה כסף. It then begins to explain רב and שמואל's reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is where he gives her food but does not give her a silver מעה for her needs. רב and שמואל hold: they enacted…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks a middle case that fits both opinions. It then starts to explain רב and שמואל's reason, and that explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each extreme case left one opinion with no reason. In the middle case the husband has met part of his duty but not all of it, so there is room to argue. The word תקנו shows the argument turns on what the חכמים enacted about a wife's earnings and her support.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (introduces the true answer)
They hold, they reason
They (the חכמים) enacted

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא finds the exact case of a dispute: it rules out both extremes until it reaches a case where each side has a real reason.

phrases.english: Really, it is where he gives her food

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ מַעֲלֶה לָהּ מָעָה כֶּסֶף לִצְרָכֶיהָ.
phrases.english: but does not give her a silver ma'a for her needs.
Rav and Shmuel hold: they enacted

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם בְּמַעֲלֶה לָהּ מְזוֹנוֹת וְאֵינוֹ מַעֲלֶה לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves both objections of steps 18 and 19 by choosing a middle case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case: a middle situation in which both opinions make sense.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute must be about either full support or no support at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is about a husband who provides food but not the מעה כסף, and the reasoning depends on what the חכמים enacted.
